review_systems.name: ACL Rolling Review October 2026 cycle
hard_gates: Use the official ACL style without modifying the style files.
Long and short papers may contain at most 8 and 4 content pages respectively.
Include a dedicated Limitations section after the conclusion and before references.
Remove author names and affiliations and anonymize supplementary materials and repository links.
Do not use download-tracking file-host links in anonymized supplementary material.
Do not submit the paper elsewhere while it is under ARR review.
Every author must complete reviewer registration within 48 hours after the submission deadline.
Keep appendices in the official double-column format and do not hide claim-critical material there.

venues.name: European Conference on Information Retrieval 2027, Full Paper Track
hard_gates: Submit a representative title and abstract by the abstract deadline.
Use the Springer LNCS proceedings template.
Keep the full paper, including appendices, within 12 pages; references are unlimited.
An accepted paper must be presented in person by a registered author.

primary.reason: The paper's core contribution is Chinese NLP information extraction and evaluation under predefined schemas; COLING's scope and the ARR contribution types directly accommodate information extraction, resources/evaluation, and NLP engineering experiments.

same_cycle_alternative.reason: It uses the same October ARR submission and ACL format, but the manuscript should make the methodological and generalization contribution especially crisp rather than read as a domain-only engineering report.

conditional_backup.reason: Use only if the paper is substantively reframed around retrieval, RAG, ontology-backed search, or retrieval evaluation; the present ontology-recognition study alone is not an IR paper.

do_not_conflate: An ARR submission is not yet a commitment to COLING or NAACL.
ARR cycle end is not automatically a venue commitment deadline.
A short paper is not interchangeable with a full or regular paper for institutional ranking rules.

style_learning.sample_scope: Nine accepted 2025 COLING/NAACL papers selected for proximity to ontology-constrained information extraction, schema alignment, event roles, knowledge-graph abstraction, prompt transfer, and evaluation design; the six papers in the project-specific COLING audit were inspected from official full-text PDFs figure by figure and table by table.
style_learning.anti_overfit_rule: Use only patterns shared across exemplars and justified by the current paper's argument; never copy wording or treat one paper's section order as a venue requirement.
style_learning.conflict_scope: This precedence resolves editorial structure, figure, and table choices only. It never overrides an official venue, review-system, ethics, anonymity, or formatting requirement.

direct_vs_adjacent.rule: Use the direct exemplars for task framing, method narrative, figure sequence, and experiment structure. Use adjacent knowledge-graph papers only for terminology and presentation patterns unless dataset, information access, schema, task, and metric are genuinely comparable.

observed_patterns: Uses Figure 1 for a realistic task example and a later figure for the method rather than forcing both jobs into one overloaded visual.
Separates fully unseen from partially seen labels in the main results.
Reports component ablation and a distinct robustness evaluation.
Bounds zero-shot claims by the information available at inference time.
Quantifies the evidence scale in the abstract and introduction instead of relying on qualitative novelty language.
Uses a functional data-and-method figure in which each operation repairs a named taxonomy failure.
Groups English, Chinese, out-of-domain, and multilingual settings instead of collapsing them into one average.
Reports repeated-run means, module-removal deltas, and scaling or perturbation evidence.
Introduces the event-role failure through a concrete example before presenting the architecture.
Maps each named module to one previously stated failure mode and carries a running example through the method figure.
Reports precision, recall, and F1, then follows the main table with module ablation and low-resource analysis.
Uses functional boxes and arrows without reducing the figure to generic software architecture.
Frames a concrete resource constraint before introducing the method.
Separates dataset construction, method, main results, and mechanism analysis.
Places dataset statistics in an early table and full prompts in the appendix.
States limitations after the conclusion.
Provides useful concept-abstraction terminology, layered method presentation, ablation, and mechanism visualization.
Does not define the same ontology-constrained extraction task and must not be presented as a direct numeric baseline.
Uses clean multilingual task framing and language- and frequency-stratified result tables.
Supports presentation and related-work framing but is not a direct baseline for ontology-constrained event extraction.
Defines the transfer boundary and controlled comparison before reporting gains.
Ablates prompt components and checks robustness to prompt paraphrases.
Uses a matched baseline and a significance test for paired predictions.
Names language, prompt sensitivity, black-box model drift, and reproducibility limits.
Gives each module a functional name tied to one failure mode.
Uses an early system overview figure and module-specific ablations.
Extends ablation analysis across difficulty, interaction conditions, and model backbones.
Moves extra ablations, case studies, and cost analysis to the appendix.
Defines datasets, splits, metrics, and compared systems before interpreting results.
Tests the method on both sentence-level and document-level event extraction.
Reports precision, recall, and F1 where extraction boundary choices matter.
States which untested mechanisms and structures limit generalization.

consensus_argument_slots: Abstract: task value, precise failure condition, task reformulation or method idea, two or three functional modules, datasets and metrics with a numeric headline, then a bounded generalization or resource implication.

Introduction: task definition plus a realistic example, two or three prior-method categories with one testable limitation each, one module mapped to each limitation, an early numeric result, then three contributions covering problem, mechanism, and evidence.
Task and method: formal inputs/outputs and allowed information, then modules named by function and connected to failure modes.

Experiments: separate fully unseen, partially seen, and cross-domain settings; use matched-information baselines, precision/recall/F1 where boundaries matter, repeated runs or confidence intervals, and reproducibility settings.

Results: main comparison first, then module ablations with local module metrics and direct deltas, schema perturbations, transfer checks, no-evidence rejection or hallucination analysis, and error slices.
Robustness: use semantically equivalent prompt rephrasings and, where feasible, multiple models or domains to distinguish a reusable design principle from lucky wording.
Conclusion and Limitations: restate only supported feasibility claims and disclose deployment, language, dataset, provider, and reproducibility boundaries.
Appendix: exact prompts and schema cards, additional per-dataset results, cases, cost, and run manifests; never exile evidence essential to the main claim.

default_figure_sequence: Figure 1: a realistic task and leakage-boundary example showing source text, evidence, candidate or neighboring schemas, allowed and forbidden information, and the target structured output.
Figure 2: a functional method chain that carries the same running example through evidence grounding, schema alignment, role-constrained extraction, and an auditable output or rejection path.
artifact_contract.combined_figure_exception: Use one combined multi-panel Figure 1 only under material page pressure or when the protocol boundary itself is the central contribution; a single overloaded first figure is not the default.
artifact_contract.functional_box_arrow_rule: Functional boxes and arrows are permitted for a method figure when every box names an intellectual operation, maps to a stated failure mode, and exposes the transformation of a concrete running example; reject generic software or platform architecture.
artifact_contract.evidence_link_rule: The evidence anchor may be distributed across the Figure 1 to Figure 2 to main-table sequence. Figure 1 does not need an embedded result metric when it already establishes the task and information boundary.
artifact_contract.table_density_rule: Four to eight rows and four to six columns is a readability heuristic, not a hard cap. Grouped multilingual, out-of-domain, unseen-label, or multi-setting matrices may be wider when headers, panels, and notes preserve readability.
